AgentResult.description:
One agent's output, plus what it cost.

The result is the agent's own schema, kept as a dict rather than typed per
agent: the shape is the JSON Schema the agent declared, Go validates against
the same one, and a second Pydantic model here would be a third place for the
three to disagree.
AgentResult.title: AgentResult

AnalyseRequest.description:
One failure, with the material an explanation may cite (BE-5.2).

``context`` is the cacheable prefix: the run log, the captured response, and the
source of the failing test. A run with forty failures analyses forty times against
the same log, so paying full price for it forty times is the difference between
this feature being affordable and not.
AnalyseRequest.title: AnalyseRequest

CacheCreateRequest.description: Creates a provider-side context cache for a fan-out.
CacheCreateRequest.title: CacheCreateRequest

CacheDeleteRequest.description: Teardown for a cache object, run at chain end including on failure.
CacheDeleteRequest.title: CacheDeleteRequest

Capabilities.description:
What a model can actually do (ai-architecture.md 3.4).

Providers are not interchangeable, and pretending otherwise produces runtime
failures a user cannot act on. Gating features on this is what turns "the model
cannot do that" into a disabled option with a reason.
Capabilities.title: Capabilities

ChatRequest.description: One completion, with everything needed to make it.

agent.description: Which agent asked, recorded on the llm_calls row.
agent.title: Agent

ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest

CodegenRequest.description: One endpoint's file, from its approved cases.
CodegenRequest.title: CodegenRequest

DedupeRequest.description: The near-miss pass. Exact duplicates never get here.
DedupeRequest.title: DedupeRequest

DesignRequest.description: One call per requirement, sharing the specification as a cached prefix.
DesignRequest.title: DesignRequest

ErrorKind.description:
Why a call failed, in terms the gateway can act on.

``retryable`` is the only kind that triggers cross-provider fallback. A
``bad_request`` retried on another provider is a bad request twice.
ErrorKind.title: ErrorKind

ErrorResponse.description: The error envelope. Mirrors Go's {code, message, details}.
ErrorResponse.title: ErrorResponse

ExtractRequest.description: Extraction reads the parsed specification, never the raw file.
ExtractRequest.title: ExtractRequest

MCPDiscoverRequest.description:
A server to connect to and list the tools of (BE-10.1).

Go owns the configuration and the credential; this carries them for one connection
and this service holds neither afterwards.
MCPDiscoverRequest.title: MCPDiscoverRequest

MCPDiscoverResponse.description: The tools a connection test found.
MCPDiscoverResponse.title: MCPDiscoverResponse

Model.description: The model to run, and what it can do.
Model.title: Model

PerfRequest.description:
A k6 load script from the API's endpoints under an authorised profile (BE-9.1).

The profile is fixed by whoever authorised the test; ``endpoints`` is the cacheable
prefix, so generating a heavier variant reuses it.
PerfRequest.title: PerfRequest

ProbeRequest.description: Confirms what a model can really do (BE-1.10).
ProbeRequest.title: ProbeRequest

ProbeResult.description:
Detected capability. It overwrites declared capability, because a
declaration is a claim and this is a measurement.
ProbeResult.title: ProbeResult

ProbeSelectRequest.description:
Which endpoints and payload IDs to point a security probe at (BE-9.3).

The catalogue carries payload IDs and purposes, never the payload strings: the
strings live in a reviewed Go library, and the agent's only job is to choose which
reviewed entry to aim where. A plan that named a raw payload would be refused.
ProbeSelectRequest.title: ProbeSelectRequest

Provider.description: One configured provider, as Go resolved it.
Provider.title: Provider

ProviderKind.description:
The provider kinds from ai-architecture.md 3.1.

``openai_compatible`` is the row that makes "any other provider" real: one
adapter covers Ollama, vLLM, LiteLLM, OpenRouter, Together, Groq, Fireworks,
and DeepSeek.
ProviderKind.title: ProviderKind

RepoStepRequest.description:
One step of a repository exploration (BE-6.4).

The tools run in Go, which owns the checkout and the path validation, so this
request carries what has been seen rather than a filesystem handle. ``tree`` is the
cacheable prefix: thirty steps over one repository are one cached prefix plus
thirty short suffixes.
RepoStepRequest.title: RepoStepRequest

ServedBy.description:
Which provider actually answered.

Recorded because a cross-provider fallback moves the cost to a different price
list, and attribution that assumed the primary would be wrong.
ServedBy.title: ServedBy

Target.description: A provider and model pair the gateway can build a client from.
Target.title: Target

TestDataRequest.description:
Realistic values for the handful of fields a faker cannot write (BE-8.2).

One call for the whole batch rather than one per record: bulk generation is
deliberately not an AI feature, and this is the narrow exception where semantics
matter.
TestDataRequest.title: TestDataRequest

Tier.description:
What a call is for, rather than which model runs it.

An agent asks for a tier. Which model serves it is a settings decision, which
is what keeps provider switching a dropdown change forever.
Tier.title: Tier

UIFlowRequest.description:
One step of a UI flow discovery (BE-7.2).

The browser lives in a worker's container, whose egress allowlist, credentials, and
reaping already govern it, so this request carries what the last action showed
rather than a browser handle. ``context`` is the cacheable prefix: forty steps
against one application are one cached prefix plus forty short suffixes.
UIFlowRequest.title: UIFlowRequest

UISpecRequest.description:
One discovered flow's Playwright spec (BE-7.4).

``graph`` is the cacheable prefix: the pages and what can be done on each do not
change between the flows of one application, so a suite is one cached prefix plus
one short instruction per flow. A regeneration after a rejected selector reuses it.
UISpecRequest.title: UISpecRequest

UnitTestRequest.description:
One untested target's test file (BE-6.5).

``source`` is the cacheable prefix: the target's own code and its neighbours. A
regeneration after a validation failure reuses it, so a correction costs a cache
read plus a short instruction rather than the whole file again.
UnitTestRequest.title: UnitTestRequest

Usage.description: What the call cost, in tokens. Go turns this into money and a row.
Usage.title: Usage

info.description: Stateless agent runner. Holds no persistence and no business logic.
info.title: Qavia AI Service

post.description:
Reasoning tier, because this is the hardest thing the platform asks a model to
do: read a log, a response body, and a test, and say which of them is wrong.

Every citation the analysis makes is checked by Go against the material before the
row is stored, and a failed check comes back here as feedback rather than being
silently accepted (BE-5.3).
post.summary: Explain why a test failed, with citations

post.description:
The envelope is schema-locked and the content is code.

Go needs the path and the covered case IDs to store the file and to trace it,
and neither can be recovered reliably from prose wrapped around a code block.
post.summary: Turn approved test cases into a runnable file

post.description:
The near-miss fallback only, on the cheap tier. Exact duplicates were
caught by a hash before this was called.
post.summary: Decide which candidates duplicate a stored case

post.description:
One requirement per call, with the specification as a cached prefix. Go
bounds how many of these run at once.
post.summary: Design test cases for one requirement

post.description:
Reads the normalized model rather than the uploaded file: deterministic
code already parsed it, and a model asked to re-read JSON structure would be
slower, cost money, and be wrong occasionally rather than never.
post.summary: Extract requirements from a parsed specification

post.description:
The load profile is a person's decision, fixed in the request; the model writes
the script that exercises the endpoints under it. Validated in the k6 image before
it makes a single request (BE-9.1).
post.summary: Generate a k6 load script under an authorised profile

post.description:
The agent picks endpoints and payload IDs from the catalogue; it never writes a
payload string. The strings live in a reviewed Go library, and a plan naming a raw
payload is refused (BE-9.3).
post.summary: Choose which endpoints and library payloads to probe

post.description:
One step, not a loop. Go executes the chosen tool against the checkout it owns
and calls back with the result, because the process that owns the filesystem is
the one that can safely validate a path (BE-6.4).
post.summary: Choose the next step of a repository exploration

post.description:
Named fields only, on the cheap tier, one call for the whole batch. The bulk of
a generated set comes from a seeded faker in Go: it is free, instant, and identical
every run, and a model asked for two thousand values would cost money to be
occasionally wrong (BE-8.2).
post.summary: Write realistic values for named fields

post.description:
One step, not a loop. The browser runs in a worker's container, so Go performs
the action and calls back with what the page looked like afterwards: the process
that owns the container is the one that can validate an action against the
vocabulary, hold the budget, and substitute a credential without showing it to a
model (BE-7.2, BE-7.3.2).
post.summary: Choose the next step of a UI flow discovery

post.description:
One call per flow, on the code tier. The selector policy is stated in the prompt
and enforced in Go afterwards: a spec that reaches for a positional selector is
rejected and regenerated rather than merged with a warning (BE-7.4.2).
post.summary: Turn one discovered flow into a Playwright spec

post.description:
One call per target, on the code tier. The framework comes from the repository's
own manifest, and the file goes through the same static validation as generated API
tests: compiled and scanned in the image that owns the toolchain (BE-3.4).
post.summary: Write a unit test for one untested target

post.description:
Only Gemini has one. Everyone else answers not-created, which is not an
error: the caller proceeds and the cost model is linear.
post.summary: Create a provider-side context cache for a fan-out

post.description:
A DELETE with a body would be the honest verb, but a cache handle and an API
key do not belong in a URL: both end up in proxy logs.

Everything an agent asks for goes through here.

Credentials arrive decrypted in the request and are used for this call only.
Usage comes back in the response and is never written here: Go owns
``llm_calls`` (backend-standards.md 10).

The connection test. Go owns the server configuration and its credential and
passes them here; this service connects via langchain-mcp-adapters, lists the tools,
and returns them so an admin can opt into specific ones (BE-10.1).
post.summary: Connect to an MCP server and list its tools

post.description: Backs the Test connection button. Detected capability overwrites declared.
post.summary: Detect what a model can actually do

get.description:
Read by the settings screen, so a build without a provider package installed
cannot offer a kind it would fail on.
get.summary: Provider kinds this build can serve
